summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 of 2: TOMMY by Joseph Hocking (Gutenberg 24986; Hodder & Stoughton, London/NY/Toronto, 1916)

**Front matter / Note (author, Feb 1916, Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts):** Author met "Tommy" before enlistment while addressing recruiting meetings for 6+ months; visited him in training camps, France and Flanders (La Bassee, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres). Says story setting is fiction, tale is fact, nearly every incident told by Tommy himself. Aim: readership of fathers, mothers, loved ones.

**Ch I (Sunday, first Sunday of June 1914, Brunford, a Lancashire cotton town):**
- Tom Pollard, weaver's son, leaves Dixon Street ~3:30 pm to Thorn and Thistle public-house (landlord Enoch Powell).
- Polly Powell (~24, buxom, bold-eyed, red-cheeked, highly coloured dresses, big feathered hats) meets him; jealous of Alice Lister; mentions Jim Scott, Jim Dixon, Jim Parkin. Says father says Tom has brains (3 prizes at Mechanics' Institute). Offers capital for a mill. Asks him back to tea.
- Tom wants to meet Alice Lister at Sunday school exit (Town Hall clock; Scott's Park, Liverpool Road).
- Alice Lister (~20, refined, contralto singer, pianist, learns French/German; father George Lister, small manufacturer, former weaver; mother Mrs. Lister). Gossip: Emily Bilson, Polly's flirtations, young landlord at Bull and Butcher.
- Alice demands Tom "make your choice": give up Thorn and Thistle or her. Mentions "Duty, God." Tom has stopped Sunday School, once teetotaler, now 22–23.
- Harry Briarfield (manufacturer's son) rumoured at Lister house.
- Harry Waterman (tall, florid, light-brown hair; claims squire's son from Warwickshire; educated in Germany; scoffs at religion) invites Tom to "club" at Rose and Crown. Tom chooses Waterman/Polly; Alice: "I see your choice is made." Parts.
- Tom home drunk; mother Martha Pollard scolds ("brazen-faaced 'uzzy"). Father Ezekiel Pollard (weaver, 30 shillings a week).

**Ch II (June 1914 to Jan 1915):**
- Brunford boom trade; Tom drifts; Polly's influence. Jim Parkin, youth warns about Polly.
- War: Crown Prince of Austria murder; Sir Edward Grey. Enoch Powell: "six weeks".
- Waterman (~Aug 1914) says Germans will win; Tom startled; Waterman walks off.
- Shweitzer (German manufacturer, Brunford) farewell dinner at Bull and Butcher; says Kaiser will rule England; Englishman punches his jaw. (Footnote: incident real in a Lancashire city.)
- Elijah Butterworth (three sons in army) challenges Tom, "coward".
- Winter 1914; Tom refuses; at Mechanics' Institute New Year recruiting meeting (speaker who had been to Belgium) Tom shouts "By God, I can't stand this!", volunteers: "No! By God, no!" Mother: "Thou'st goin' for a sodger."

**Ch III:**
- Tom tells Polly at midnight; she's unimpressed ("Thou'st noan been such a fool?"); Tom asks her to stay true.
- Alice meets Tom at Town Hall morning, praises him, "we shall be praying for you." Mention of young parson after Alice.
- Joins Loyal North Lancashires (battalion unnamed; Lancashire town ~30 miles from Brunford; later camp in Surrey, May 1915). Deteriorates: drunk and disorderly; punished.
- Robert Penrose (Cornish, Charterhouse-educated, private, later commissioned; boxer; attends Y.M.C.A. for French with a Frenchman). Tells Tom about Y.M.C.A.
- Alec McPhail (Scottish, Black Watch, ex-whisky drinker, father an elder in U.P. Kirk, mother godly; read Ingersoll; "Shorter Catechism").
- Colonel (stern, kindly) punishes; "Make a beast of myself"; recommends Y.M.C.A.
- Tom attends Y.M.C.A.; French "Je suis / Vous etes / Nous sommes / Ils sont".
- Surrey camp (May 1915): Tom leave; drinks with Polly (ginger ale refused, takes beer). Battalion 1,100 strong; ~30,000 men in camp.
- Meets Lt. Waterman (commissioned) in camp.

**Ch IV (Surrey camp, then Folkestone, Boulogne):**
- Interview with narrator: Tom's French report; Y.M.C.A. huts.
- Mother's letter (Polly walking out with Jim Dixon; "sack her"; "If you come across that German Emperor, don't be soft-hearted wi' 'im").
- Alec McPhail gives heart to God; farewell Y.M.C.A. meeting speaker ("Captain, Guide, Saviour"); canteen scene; pale lad's mother praying.
- Folkestone troopship, Boulogne, troop train, then guns; "I wonder now——".

**Ch V (Ypres salient):**
- Sergeant (served 20 years; two bullets; "Jack Johnson and Black Maria"; "Wipers"; poison gas). Ruined Ypres (Cloth Hall, Cathedral). Trenches: Piccadilly, Haymarket, Bond Street, Whitehall.
- Lancashire boy shot through brain by sniper. Officer: "Hampstead Heath Bank Holiday skylarking."
- Bombardment; bayonet charge; young officer rescues German who shoots him with revolver. (Footnote: real incident.)
- Tom's sentry night; prays "O God!" repeatedly. Thinks of Alice praying.
- Friends named: Jim Bates, Arthur Wadge, Bill Perkins, George Wilson (killed).

**Ch VI (same night):** Alice Lister's point of view. Harry Briarfield (24, partner in father George Briarfield's business) proposes; Alice asks 3 days. Mr. Lister: "our Alice... Harry's a nice lad." Mrs. Lister: "you can never judge a lass's heart"; mentions William Pott. Mr. Skelton (young minister) proposed earlier, refused. Alice prays "O God, save him!" at midnight (Town Hall clock).

**Ch VII:**
- German voice from trench (night): "you Lancashires are going to attack at six o'clock to-morrow, eleven hundred strong." Tom reports to subaltern; Colonel; Major Blundell; Sergeant Ashworth vouches for Tom. Attack made; Black Watch brought up; trap known. Tom's conversion: "I felt God spoke to me."
- Alec McPhail wounded; Tom visits hospital (near Ypres, road to Cassel); nurse. McPhail dies; Psalm 23 recited; hymn "Jesu, Lover of my soul." McPhail: "It's a' richt."

**Ch VIII:**
- Colonel Blount and Major Blundell discuss treachery; General Withers (Divisional HQ). Achan in camp. Tom suspects; Water Tower; saw staff officer (Waterman).
- Night at Potijze Road: Tom sees Waterman throw white paper with a stone-like weight across to German lines, with signal cry. Tom tackles; Lt. Penrose and Lt. Jackson arrive; Major Blundell. Tom crawls into No-man's-Land; wrestles German; breaks his shoulder with football trick; wounded in left arm and right shoulder; reaches trench; "Have you got it?" Doctor: "simply a miracle." Colonel Blount visits; "shoot him."

**Ch IX:** Court-martial; Waterman admits being German (Waterman, born to German parents; two n's in name; "Fatherland"; "I have counted the cost"). Shot at a wall next morning. Tom recommended for D.C.M.

**Ch X (late Nov 1915 to Dec 1915):** Newspapers "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad." Mrs. Pollard comments; Ezekiel. Tom home on leave, Saturday in Dec; Polly at station ("I have not got any young men"); Rose and Crown refused ("following the example of the King"). Parents kneel together and pray.

**Ch XI:** Sunday evening church with parents; meets Alice in vestibule; walk up Liverpool Road to lane. Alice never engaged to Harry Briarfield. Tom asks her to wait. Lister approves (Mrs. Lister: "yon's a grand lad"). Waterloo station goodbye; Kipling's "The Ship That Found Herself"; "au revoir." Narrator saw him off. Closing: "God help me to do my bit."

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: OUT OF THE BLUE by Bertrand W. Sinclair (Gutenberg 73542; Blue Book Magazine, July 7, 1927)

**Ch I (A Retaining Fee, Fort Worth, April):**
- Rock Holloway (young Texas range rider; sorrel horse Sangre; gray Stetson; buckskin gloves; silver-inlaid saddle; reata; went to eastern university briefly; father Steve Holloway, ex-U.S. marshal at Abilene; mother; sister Cecilia (Cissy) marrying a Brett of B X, El Paso; uncle Tom Holloway (ranger captain, "Long Tom"); cousin Ben Holloway, Ragged H on Milk River).
- Trinity Bank (graffiti "Holy"); "Uncle Bill" Sayre (banker, cattleman, speaks dialect "yo'"), Marcus Proud, Abel Stewart.
- Sayre: Seventy Seven trail herd (Duffy outfit) going North; Duffy brothers Joe, Elmer (trail boss), Ed, Mark (big, bully). Maltese Cross (Dave Snell's outfit, Trinity west fork, ~30,000 cattle; moved to Montana, Marias River, near Fort Benton). Dave Snell died; leaves estate to daughter Alice (21) and son (16). Executors: Sayre and "Buck" Walters (range boss, young, high-handed, fond of women, poker). $500 advance in gold; $60/month. Retaining fee.
- Rock: "Sangre" addressed.

**Ch II (Clark's Ford, Nebraska, July, the Odeon dance hall):**
- Al Kerr (Waco cattleman, tiny, gnome-faced, Capital K, Judith Basin on Arrow Creek, Lewistown P.O.).
- Mark Duffy drinks at bar; lifts Kerr onto bar; threatens with gun; shoots at floor. Rock intervenes; Duffy draws, Rock shoots him dead. Rock leaves with Kerr's riders. Rock now fears Duffy feud.

**Ch III (The Steering Wheel):** Journey North; Rock joins Steering Wheel (wagon boss; Canada, Fort MacLeod; Old Man River). Dave Wells (Texan, tall, thin, drawly) runs outfit; 4 riders discharged; suspicious doggies (fresh Steering Wheel burn on cattle with blurred other brands). Rock leaves April/June. Sweet Grass Hills, Fort Benton route.

**Ch IV (A Dead Double):** Rock packs mules for U.S. cavalry near Milk River (Fort Assiniboine). Reaches Marias valley; Parke ranch (TL brand): Nona Parke (~20, dark hair, gray eyes, deep voice, educated), daughter Betty (3, blonde, blue eyes, rag doll, calls him "Doc"). Dead man Doc Martin (cowboy, shot from ambush by river; looks like Rock). Nona's mother died at Betty's birth; father (Parke) died after horse fell on him. Snow winter. Nona: "Elmer Duffy" suspected. Rock sleeps in stable.

**Ch V (Wrapped in Canvas):** Burial of Doc Martin next to Parke graves under cottonwood; wrapped in canvas.

**Ch VI (Very Adroit Rock):** Nona hires Rock at $50/month (rules: no sentiment). Elmer Duffy rides up; Rock poses as Doc Martin; Elmer thinks he is Doc; Rock says "Up the river somebody took a pot shot at me." Elmer denies; accepts. Rock decides to pose as Doc. Nona: half-breed girl Mary Vieux (16, nurse), Charlie Shaw (Parke rider, ~20, blue eyes, slender, smiling).

**Ch VII (Mariners):** Rock rides round-up; meets TL rider Charlie Shaw and Alice Snell (yellow hair, blue-purple eyes, split green corduroy skirt, carved saddle; "rep" for Maltese Cross); Buck Walters (agate-gray eyes, tall, flashy); Rock gets glare. Alice: Nona "never lets grass grow." Nona: Alice "good-looking"; Alice detests Buck. Rock feels attraction to Nona. Nona's calves missing (~60–70). Rock's uncertainty.

**Ch VIII (Getting Down to Cases):** Charlie: rustling rumors about Rock and Burris boys (behind the Goosebill, rawhide neckties). Buck wants Doc out of way for Alice. Charlie reveals Buck's hard men (Killer types). Charlie reveals identity to Charlie: Rock shows bloodstained saddle, room with Doc's gear. Nona: hay for winter.

**Ch IX (Ordered South):** Rock to Fort Benton (old fur post, Grand Union Hotel); sees Buck Walters & Dave Wells at bar. Rock identifies himself as Rock Holloway to Wells; Walters denies; Rock says he is Doc Martin. Night: Walters warns Rock "go South" "48 hours"; threatens. Rock punches? (No; he refrains because of Wells.)

**Ch X (Thirty Angry Men):** Alice Snell rides warning: Walters and Elmer Duffy plus crew coming to hang Doc for "stealing." Rock stands in doorway with carbine; Nona shields Alice. Charlie Shaw inside; Rock reveals identity; Elmer deduces "Rock Holloway" (killed Mark). Walters accuses Doc of Burris rustling; Alice accuses Walters of killing Doc ("You were afraid of him"). Mob leaves.

**Ch XI (Riders on a Rise):** Nona/Rock talk; "You steal hearts." Charlie explains Walters' rustling; Charlie & Rock ride for work horses; two riders on rise; ambush in ravine: Rock's horse shot; second assassin fled. Rock catches Stack (Joe Stack) hog-tied; other is Bill Hurley (dead). Maltese Cross horses.

**Ch XII (Stack Decides to Talk):** Rock's head wound (scalp). Rock torments Stack with fire (burns foot); Stack confesses: Buck offered $500 to kill Rock; Hurley shot Doc Martin. Buck going north with crew. Rock releases Stack on Maltese horse, saddle returned.

**Ch XIII (On the Warpath):** Nona dresses Rock's head (carbolic). Walters' crew leaves for North (Sweet Grass). Rock kisses Nona before leaving at dawn ("hell of a way for a fellow to treat a girl"). Rock rides to Judith Basin, Kerr ranch; Kerr offers men; Kerr knows Sayre, loaned him $20,000.

**Ch XIV (Hot on the Trail):** Rock telegraphs Sayre from Billings (N.P. Hotel); Sayre replies: "Act on your own judgment. Will back any action you take. Suspected this. Coming north, first train." Rock with Capital K riders; meets Charlie Shaw at camp: Charlie found hidden corrals (branding pens) at Sweet Grass Hills; Walters camped on creek, five riders joined from North; Steering Wheel brand.

**Ch XV (Popping Guns):** East Butte of Sweet Grass Hills; corrals (dumb-bell shape); Walters, Dave Wells, six riders rebranding Maltese Cross to Steering Wheel. Charlie shot off a bank by lookout; falls over edge. Rock flees on horse; horse shot; Rock shoots Walters at 20 yards; Walters' black horse charges and falls on Rock (injured leg; furrow under armpit). Rock's Capital K riders arrive.

**Ch XVI ("Certainly Not Sad"):** Maltese Cross herd branded with Steering Wheel; Capital K horses; Buck and Wells dead; Uncle Bill Sayre at Maltese Cross house; Rock explains (paper marks showing Maltese Cross → steering wheel; Buck borrowed $25,000 for 1,200 head cattle from Panhandle). Sayre asks Rock to run Maltese Cross; Rock "I'll tell you tomorrow." Elmer Duffy and Rock shake hands. Charlie shot but alive (sent to Benton). Rock tells Nona; Nona: "I am glad that man is dead." Rock kisses; Nona: "I like you a heap." Tears: "there are two times when every woman cries... And I'm certainly not sad!" End.
